title: Bulgogi-style marinade
summary: A savoury-sweet Korean-style marinade of tamari, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and scallion for thinly sliced beef.
steps: Stir everything together until the erythritol dissolves.
Slice 900 g (2 lb) of ribeye or sirloin as thinly as you can across the grain (partly freezing it for 30 minutes makes this easy).
Toss the beef with the marinade and refrigerate 1–4 hours.
Cook in batches in a very hot, lightly oiled pan or over a hot grill, 1–2 minutes per side, so it sears rather than stews. Scatter with more scallion and sesame seeds.
tips: Traditional bulgogi marinade includes grated Asian pear, which also tenderises; it is left out here for its sugar.
For a soy-free version use coconut aminos instead of tamari, but it carries about 20 g of carbs per 100 g, so use 3 tbsp plus 2 tbsp water and skip the erythritol.
The carbs shown count the whole batch; only what clings to the meat is eaten, so the real figure per serving is lower.

origin.history: Bulgogi, 'fire meat', is thinly sliced marinated beef grilled quickly over high heat. Korean writers often trace it to older grilled-meat dishes such as maekjeok, said to date back to the Goguryeo kingdom, though that lineage is a tradition rather than a documented line. The name bulgogi itself is a twentieth-century term, and the dish became one of the best-known Korean foods abroad in the late 1900s.
